title: What lies beyond the Fields Medal? | Science
abstract: The International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM), a quadrennial conference dating back to the 19th century, kicks off today in Philadelphia, PA, USA. The highlight of the opening ceremony is the announcement of a new cohort of Fields medalists. The award is often described as the Nobel Prize of mathematics, but Fields medalists are conspicuously younger than Nobel Laureates, who typically conduct their award-winning research in chemistry, economics, medicine, or physics in their mid-40s and receive the award decades later. Mathematicians are only eligible for the Fields Medal until the year they turn 40. Why is mathematics' highest honor reserved exclusively for the young?

title: Protect and expand ocean observation systems | Science
abstract: The United States alone is responsible for roughly half of the world’s ocean monitoring platforms (1). In May, the US government announced plans to decommission and remove more than 900 deep-sea instruments moored across the Atlantic and Pacific oceans (2). Although implementation has since been paused (3), the episode exposed the vulnerability of a global ocean observation system that is essential to global risk management infrastructure. The international community must take urgent steps to broaden the coalition of countries investing in ocean observation infrastructure.

title: Seafood biosecurity gaps threaten biodiversity | Science
abstract: Biological invasions pose serious threats to biodiversity, ecosystem function, economies, and human health (1). Live seafood trading is a major pathway for the introduction of non-native and invasive species (2–5). Although existing local and global frameworks align with international treaties, regulations are often outdated, weakly enforced, and inconsistent across countries (6–9). To address these gaps, a more robust and coordinated approach is needed to reinforce existing biosecurity protocols.
